claims.statement: Agentic AI engineering owns the deterministic action loop and its evidence, while product, platform, domain, safety, and security authorities retain their own decisions.
A useful engineering distinction is that workflows follow predefined control flow while agents let a model materially direct tool use and execution toward a goal.
The least autonomous architecture that meets task and control requirements should be the baseline against which an agent is justified.
The general claim that adding multiple agents improves task quality is unsupported; any benefit is task-specific and must be measured against coordination and resource cost.
A delegated task needs an observable completion predicate, bounded allowed actions, consequence classes, budgets, stop and escalation rules, and named authority before effectful execution.
Confirmation and oversight are risk controls for consequential actions but do not transfer formal authority or guarantee correct action.
